quests.question: ___ the roads were dangerously icy, officials made the decision to delay school by one day.
quests.hint: This introduces the reason behind a decision, in a tone more formal than 'because'.
quests.explanation: 'As' can introduce a reason in formal writing — the icy roads are the reason for the delay.

quests.question: The board hasn't decided ___ to approve the merger ___ reject it.
quests.hint: Two possible decisions are both still being considered.
quests.explanation: 'Whether...or' introduces two possible outcomes under consideration — approval or rejection.

quests.question: Two employees called in sick, ___ the shift was short-staffed all day.
quests.hint: Absences directly caused a staffing problem.
quests.explanation: 'So' introduces a result — the sick employees caused the shortage.

quests.question: The hike was exhausting, ___ the view from the summit made it worthwhile.
quests.hint: A real difficulty is acknowledged, but something made it worth it anyway.
quests.explanation: 'Though' introduces a concession, like 'although' — the tiring hike was still worth it for the view.

quests.question: No sooner had the meeting started ___ the fire alarm went off.
quests.hint: This fixed expression always pairs 'no sooner' with one specific word — not 'when'.
quests.explanation: 'No sooner...than' is a fixed pair showing one event immediately followed by another.

quests.question: She switched to a plant-based diet ___ her cholesterol levels were too high.
quests.hint: A specific medical result explains the dietary change.
quests.explanation: 'Because' gives the direct reason for a decision — high cholesterol led to the diet change.

quests.question: We'll board the connecting flight ___ our first flight lands.
quests.hint: Boarding follows landing immediately, without delay.
quests.explanation: 'As soon as' means immediately after — boarding follows landing without delay.

quests.question: ___ it was raining heavily, the match continued without any delay.
quests.hint: A full clause with a subject and verb follows the blank — one common word cannot be used here.
quests.explanation: 'Although' introduces a full clause here. 'Despite' cannot be followed by a subject and verb — it needs a noun phrase instead.

quests.question: The airline lost our luggage, ___ they delivered it to our hotel the next day.
quests.hint: A problem was followed by a fix that resolved it.
quests.explanation: 'But' introduces a contrast — losing the luggage was followed by a surprising resolution.

quests.question: ___ the grandchildren arrive, dinner will already be on the table.
quests.hint: One event will already be complete before the other one happens.
quests.explanation: 'By the time' shows dinner will be ready before the grandchildren's arrival.

quests.question: The family reunion won't happen this year ___ someone volunteers to organize it.
quests.hint: One missing role is the only thing standing in the way.
quests.explanation: 'Unless' means 'except if' — the reunion depends entirely on this one condition.

quests.question: ___ both grandparents are getting older, the family visits more often now.
quests.hint: This word can introduce a reason, not just a starting point in time.
quests.explanation: 'Since' can mean 'because' when introducing a reason — the grandparents' age explains the more frequent visits.

quests.question: The town keeps extra sandbags ready ___ the river floods again.
quests.hint: You're preparing for something that might happen, not something certain.
quests.explanation: 'In case' introduces a precaution for a possible event — the sandbags are ready if flooding happens.

quests.question: Some residents want a new park, ___ others prefer better road repairs.
quests.hint: Two different opinions are placed side by side.
quests.explanation: 'While' contrasts two different opinions within the same community.

quests.question: The petition gathered thousands of signatures, ___ the council agreed to review it.
quests.hint: Strong public support directly led to an official response.
quests.explanation: 'So' introduces a result — the large petition caused the council's decision to review it.

quests.question: ___ the software update finishes installing, the computer will restart automatically.
quests.hint: Finishing the installation is the trigger for the next automatic step.
quests.explanation: 'Once' means 'as soon as this is complete' — finishing the update triggers the restart.

quests.question: The website crashed ___ too many users tried to log in at once.
quests.hint: A specific traffic problem explains the crash.
quests.explanation: 'Because' gives the direct reason for the crash — the surge of users logging in.

quests.question: IT still hasn't confirmed ___ the outage was caused by a hack ___ a simple server error.
quests.hint: Two possible causes are both still under investigation.
quests.explanation: 'Whether...or' introduces two possible explanations under consideration — a hack or a server error.

quests.question: ___ the flu season had started early, the clinic extended its opening hours.
quests.hint: This introduces a reason, similar to 'because', in a more formal tone.
quests.explanation: 'As' introduces a reason here — the early flu season explains the extended hours.

quests.question: The surgery was minor, ___ the recovery still took several weeks.
quests.hint: A small detail is acknowledged, but something else took longer than expected.
quests.explanation: 'Though' introduces a concession — a minor surgery still required a longer recovery.

quests.question: You shouldn't take this medication ___ a doctor has prescribed it.
quests.hint: A prescription is the one requirement here.
quests.explanation: 'Unless' means 'except if' — taking the medication safely depends on this one condition.

quests.question: ___ the marketing budget was tight, the campaign still performed very well.
quests.hint: What follows the blank is a complete clause, with its own subject and verb.
quests.explanation: 'Although' introduces a full clause here — 'despite' would instead need a noun phrase, like 'despite the tight budget'.

quests.question: The interview went well, ___ she still felt nervous about the result.
quests.hint: A positive outcome didn't fully calm her nerves.
quests.explanation: 'But' introduces a contrast — a good interview didn't remove the nervous feeling.

quests.question: Managers hold weekly check-ins ___ small problems don't turn into big ones.
quests.hint: Holding check-ins has a clear, intended purpose.
quests.explanation: 'So that' introduces a purpose — the check-ins are meant to catch problems early.

quests.question: You can change your seat online ___ you do it before check-in closes.
quests.hint: Doing it before check-in closes is the specific window for this option.
quests.explanation: 'As long as' means 'on the condition that' — changing seats online depends on this timing.

quests.question: ___ we found a parking spot, the flight had already started boarding.
quests.hint: One event was already happening before the other one finished.
quests.explanation: 'By the time' shows boarding had already started before they finished parking.

quests.question: The itinerary looked exhausting on paper, ___ the trip felt perfectly relaxed.
quests.hint: A tiring-looking plan led to a surprisingly calm result.
quests.explanation: 'Yet' shows surprising contrast — an exhausting-looking plan still felt relaxed in practice.

quests.question: The community garden thrived ___ volunteers watered it every single day.
quests.hint: Consistent effort explains the garden's success.
quests.explanation: 'Because' gives the direct reason for a result — daily watering caused the garden to thrive.

quests.question: The new bridge is not only faster to cross ___ also much safer for cyclists.
quests.hint: 'Not only' always pairs with one word to add a second benefit.
quests.explanation: 'Not only...but also' adds a second benefit to the first — speed and safety.

quests.question: The vote won't be valid ___ at least half the members take part.
quests.hint: Reaching half participation is the one requirement here.
quests.explanation: 'Unless' means 'except if' — a valid vote depends entirely on this one condition.
